item.title: The Left Ripple of Byte-Pair Encoding: Certified Lookbehind for Every Dictionary
item.description: arXiv:2611.13061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Berglund and van der Merwe formalized byte-pair encoding and bounded how far an appended string can change a tokenization, leaving the converse open: how far can a string prepended on the left change it, which dictionaries make that ripple infinite, and can it be computed efficiently when finite? We answer all three for every dictionary. The origin radius, how far a prepend can change covering spans, is decided with radius certificates by a product of two runs of the automaton that guesses the final tokens, in time polynomial in the dictionary written out, and it is infinite exactly when one periodic word has two canonical tilings with no common boundary. Under their ordering condition it is infinite exactly when some rule (t, t) finds its two copies adjacent at its own stage, and such a rule makes any dictionary infinite. A finite radius makes every window of a width read off the radii have a cut, and the radius is finite exactly when such cuts are dense. The token machine completes for every dictionary, and the tokenization is subsequential, extending what Berglund, Martens and van der Merwe proved for proper ones under one pass per rule. A streaming tokenizer emits after every symbol exactly the tokens that no continuation changes, in polynomial time, answering a question of Dalirrooyfard and Ye. Boundedness of the label measure, the edit distance of the token sequences, is decided for every dictionary in polynomial time as well, and under the ordering condition the largest distance one edit causes over dictionaries of m rules lies asymptotically between m^2/10 and m^2/2. GPT-2's merge table carries 244 effective self-pairs, so its origin radius is infinite from the forty-second merge on, and that of cl100k, o200k and Llama 3 from their first. Every measured number is its program's output, and what is not executed is named.
item.dc:creator: Nicklas Nidh\"ogg

item.title: A Unary-to-Nonunary Transition in the Accepting-State Spectrum of Right Quotient for Permutation Automata
item.description: arXiv:2605.10852v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper determines the accepting-state spectrum of the right-quotient operation for permutation automata, solving an open problem posed by Rauch and Holzer. They showed that in the unary case in which the languages whose right quotient we consider are languages over an alphabet with but one symbol, the accepting state complexities which could ensue for automata recognizing their quotient is exactly all integers between $1$ and $mn$ inclusive when $m,n \ge 1$; we show that for arbitrary alphabets the accepting-state spectrum is $g^{\operatorname{asc}}_{-1,\mathrm{PFA}}(m,n)=\{0\}$ if $m=0$ or $n=0$, and $g^{\operatorname{asc}}_{-1,\mathrm{PFA}}(m,n)=\mathbb{N}_{>0}$ if $m,n\ge 1$. Our result shows that every positive accepting-state complexity ensues for right quotient as long as both of the languages of which we consider the right quotient are nonempty. $0$ becomes the only unavoidable magic value. Moreover, we show that an alphabet with just two letters can witness any arbitrary $\alpha \ge 1$ when $m,n \ge 1$, in that languages can be defined over a binary alphabet with accepting-state complexity $m$ and $n$ respectively for which their right quotient has accepting-state complexity $\alpha$. What ultimately happens in our proof is that we construct $(A^{\mathrm q}_{m,\alpha},B^{\mathrm q}_{n,\alpha})$ such that the words accepted by $B^{\mathrm q}_{n,\alpha}$ induce a point stabilizer in a symmetric group, and the standard quotient construction giving an automaton recognizing the quotient language then saturates the original final set of $A^{\mathrm q}_{m,\alpha}$ to a full orbit; this gives a minimal quotient automaton with exactly $\alpha$ final states. The complete spectrum which is our result follows from this, solving the open question of what the right quotient's accepting-state complexity for permutation automata is.

item.title: Exact Accepting-State Spectrum for Reversal of Permutation Automata
item.description: arXiv:2605.13385v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we determine the accepting-state spectrum of the reversal operation on permutation automata, and moreover prove the conjecture conjectured by Rauch and Holzer in so doing. Namely, we show that reversal satisfies the spectrum $g^{\operatorname{asc}}_{R,\mathrm{PFA}}(0)=\{0\}$, $g^{\operatorname{asc}}_{R,\mathrm{PFA}}(1)=\{1\}$, and $g^{\operatorname{asc}}_{R,\mathrm{PFA}}(m)=\mathbb{N}_{\ge 2}$ for $m\ge 2$. We do this by, for every $m\ge 2$ and every $\alpha\ge 2$, constructing a binary permutation automaton $A_{m,\alpha}$ such that $ \operatorname{asc}(L(A_{m,\alpha}))=m$ and $ \operatorname{asc}(L(A_{m,\alpha})^{R})=\alpha$. The spectrum above follows from this (combined with the trivial cases $m=0$ and $m=1$ and the fact that $1$ is magic for every $m\ge 2$). Thus our result shows that for $m \ge 2$, the reversal operation in permutation automaton attains ever single value positive value in the accepting-state complexity except for $1$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: 27th International Conference on Descriptional Complexity of Formal Systems (DCFS 2026), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 16681, pp. 74-82, Springer (2027)

item.title: An exact compress-with-another threshold in a binary automaton family
item.description: arXiv:2610.07044v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a state $q$ in a synchronizing automaton, let $\mu(q)$ be the minimum length of a word merging $q$ with another initial state. Szyku{\l}a asked whether $\mu(q)=O(n)$ for strongly connected synchronizing automata and described a binary family attributed to D\.{z}yga, with $n=3p$ states and a conjectured threshold $4n/3$. We specify the boundary transitions omitted from the published piecewise definition and prove that the resulting automata $\mathcal A_p$ satisfy $\mu(q_0)=4p=4n/3$ for all $p\geq3$. A shortest word merging $q_0$ with another state is $(ba)^p(ab)^p$. We also construct a reset word of length $3p^2+4p-1$. Consequently, any uniform linear upper bound for $\mu(q)$ on binary strongly connected synchronizing automata with corank-one letters has leading constant at least $4/3$.
item.dc:creator: Qichao Wang, Daoyu Dong

item.title: Block-exchange descent for insertion: commuting projections and minimum masks
item.description: arXiv:2610.39941v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For fixed nonempty words $u,v$, the minimum insertion degree of a shuffle is the least number of inserted-source runs among its representations. We prove that, after a block exchange from a minimum mask of degree $r$, the minimum over masks with commuting source projections is exactly $r-1$; a larger decrease occurs precisely when a noncommuting mask has fewer runs. If either source is unary, every such exchange is exact. We prove an explicit repair for an infinite periodic degree-three family. Computer-assisted results establish first-mask descent through combined length seventeen over every alphabet, degree-three first-mask descent through length thirty, and a uniform repair of all degree-three failures through length thirty, including all further letter identifications. Counterexamples to arbitrary, first, and last minimum-mask choices explain the need for alternative masks. Finally, we prove that minimum iteration depths have no gaps for arbitrary languages. General block-exchange descent and Singleton No-Gap remain open.
item.dc:creator: Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang, Charles E. Hughes
